case_types.name: Cheque bounce
case_types.blurb: Dishonour of a cheque for insufficiency of funds - a criminal complaint. Around 15% of a typical court's caseload; high volume, relatively standard.

attribution.originalSource: as relayed by Mehul; ultimate source likely court staff or field observation

practice_notes.statement: In Kerala a scrutiny officer reviews litigant and advocate submissions and marks defects before the file is sent for taking cognizance. Reportedly the role is informal and not in the rules, and the officer often does not mark defects properly, holding files so the advocate approaches him and may make a payment to move the file forward.

claims.claim: a defect-scrutiny step happens before cognizance
the scrutiny role is informal and not in the rules
claims.note: Scrutiny is a formal function: the Registry scrutinises filings and notes objections under E-Filing Rules r.17, and CRP r.68 requires defective petitions to be returned for amendment and representation. Only the specific title 'scrutiny officer' and the file-holding-for-payment fall outside the rules.

claims.claim: files are held so the advocate pays to move them
claims.toCheck: not established as fact; needs field corroboration - who, how often, which courts

rollout_states.name: Kerala
rollout_states.note: Mostly individuals and small companies filing. The original clean-sheet pilot - ~2,000 cases/yr in Kollam. Court language: Malayalam.

rollout_states.name: Gujarat
rollout_states.note: High share of institutional filers - banks and NBFCs - sometimes a thousand cases in a day. Needs bulk filing and case management at scale. Court language: Gujarati.

rollout_states.name: Punjab
rollout_states.note: Requirements captured; own sequencing of the same shared-core process.

rollout_states.note: Early engagement - a small jurisdiction with its own local practice.
